question: What is the main thing that decides how dangerous or toxic a substance will be in the body?
explanation: You've got this! In toxicology, the golden rule is that 'the dose makes the poison.' Even safe things can become harmful if the amount is too high. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h1)

question: An unconscious patient is found next to an open container of insecticide. How did the poison most likely enter their body?
explanation: Spot on! Farming chemicals and insecticides are easily breathed in as fumes or absorbed straight through the skin when spilled. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h1)

question: Why do toddlers in many Nigerian homes frequently experience accidental kerosene poisoning?

options.A: Direct prescription of fuel by traditional healers
options.B: Storage of fuel in empty beverage bottles
options.C: Lack of electricity in rural communities
options.D: Selling of medicine in open markets

explanation: Great clinical insight! When kerosene is kept in empty soft drink bottles, kids easily mistake it for a drink and swallow it. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h2)

question: A farmer comes to the clinic with too much saliva, tearing eyes, and muscle twitching after spraying crops. What kind of poison caused this?
explanation: Well done! Organophosphates affect nerve signals by stopping acetylcholinesterase, leading to an overload of body secretions and muscle twitching. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h2)

question: How does carbon monoxide poisoning harm the body's tissues?

options.A: By directly destroying the walls of the stomach
options.B: By causing immediate paralysis of skeletal muscles
options.C: By blocking the absorption of glucose in the gut
options.D: By binding to hemoglobin and preventing oxygen delivery

explanation: Spot on! Carbon monoxide attaches to red blood cells even tighter than oxygen, leaving your tissues gasping for air. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h3)

question: Why is taking too much paracetamol so dangerous specifically for the liver?

options.A: It stops the heart from pumping blood to the abdominal organs
options.B: It causes severe dehydration by halting kidney filtration entirely
options.C: It triggers immediate bleeding inside the stomach lining
options.D: It creates a toxic metabolic byproduct that destroys liver cells

explanation: You're doing great! When paracetamol overload happens, the liver creates a harsh chemical byproduct called NAPQI that attacks and destroys liver cells. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h3)

question: What kind of changes in the eyes (pupils) do you expect to see in someone with an opioid overdose?
explanation: Spot on! A classic sign of opioid overdose is very tiny, pinpoint pupils (known as miosis). It's a quick clue to look out for on the ward! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h4)

question: Which of these symptoms is NOT part of a typical anticholinergic poisoning (toxidrome)?
explanation: Well thought out! Anticholinergic drugs actually dry up the body's secretions, so the patient will have dry skin instead of sweating. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h4)

question: What is the main job of activated charcoal when given to someone who swallowed a poison?

options.A: It binds to toxins in the gut to prevent absorption
options.B: It speeds up bowel movements to clear waste quickly
options.C: It neutralizes stomach acid to protect the lining
options.D: It causes immediate vomiting to empty the stomach

explanation: You got it! Activated charcoal acts like a magnet in the tummy, holding onto the poison so it cannot enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h5)

question: When should you NOT perform gastric lavage (pumping the stomach) on a poisoned patient?

options.A: If the ingested medication is a small white pill
options.B: Ingestion of corrosive acids or petroleum products
options.C: When the patient arrived within thirty minutes
options.D: When the patient is fully awake and cooperative

explanation: Brilliant! Never pump the stomach if the patient swallowed fuel or acid, because bringing it back up can burn the airway or cause them to breathe it into their lungs. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h5)

question: Which medication is the specific antidote used for a serious paracetamol overdose?
explanation: Spot on! N-acetylcysteine is a lifesaver here; it protects the liver by boosting glutathione to clear out the toxic paracetamol breakdown products. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h6)

question: How does naloxone manage to quickly revive someone having an opioid overdose?

options.A: It forces the kidneys to filter out the drug within minutes
options.B: It coats the lining of the stomach to stop further absorption
options.C: It attaches to opioid receptors and blocks the drug's action
options.D: It speeds up metabolism to burn off the extra medication

explanation: You're a star! Naloxone is a fast-acting blocker that kicks opioids off their receptors, quickly waking the patient and helping them breathe again. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h6)

question: What is a major nursing duty when looking after a patient admitted after an intentional self-poisoning?

options.A: Ensuring a safe environment free from harmful objects
options.B: Insisting the patient explain their reasons for self-harm
options.C: Discharging the patient immediately after waking up
options.D: Restricting all family members from visiting forever

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the patient safe is our number one duty. We always check the room and remove anything they could use to try self-harming again. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h7)

question: Why is monitoring hourly urine output so important when caring for a severe poisoning case?

options.A: To evaluate kidney perfusion and clearance of toxins
options.B: To calculate exact fluid intake requirements for meals
options.C: To check if the patient is drinking enough clean water
options.D: To prevent urinary tract infections during bed rest

explanation: Well done! Good urine output tells us the kidneys are getting enough blood flow and are successfully flushing the toxins out of the body. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h7)

question: What is the safest way to store household cleaning products and kerosene at home?

options.A: In locked cupboards high up and out of reach of children
options.B: In empty mineral water bottles near the kitchen cooking stove
options.C: On the floor right beside the kitchen door for easy access
options.D: Inside low plastic baskets where toddlers play with toys

explanation: Spot on! Always keep chemicals in their original containers and locked away high up where curious little hands cannot reach them. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h8)

question: Which community nursing action is best for stopping accidental poisoning in young children?

options.A: Treating snakebites using traditional herbal methods
options.B: Providing free prescription drugs to every household
options.C: Building emergency clinics in rural farming districts
options.D: Educating mothers on proper household chemical storage

explanation: You nailed it! Prevention is key in public health. Teaching caregivers safe storage habits stops accidental poisonings before they ever happen. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h8)
